questions.stem: In the world of data solutions, what does Accessibility pertain to?
options: Your ability to connect to and utilise data for decision-making purposes
A comprehensive understanding of what is happening behind the scenes with your data
The physical location of the servers
The cost of storing the data
The speed of the network connection
questions.explanation: Accessibility pertains to your ability to connect to and utilise data for decision-making purposes.

options: Being granted read privileges on a database
Having a comprehensive understanding of what is happening behind the scenes with your data
Seeing the database on a network map
Having a dashboard with bright colours
Being able to log into the data warehouse
questions.explanation: Visibility involves having a comprehensive understanding of what is happening behind the scenes with your data.

questions.stem: How is Accessibility achieved in practice?
options: By reading the data lineage documentation
By learning the business rules used for transformations
When the database administrator or datastore owner grants you privileges to read, write or update your data
By reviewing the data quality assurance methods
By knowing the SLAs of the loading process
questions.explanation: Accessibility is achieved when your database administrator or datastore owner grants you privileges within the database, allowing you to read, write or update your data.

questions.stem: Which of the following contributes to Visibility rather than Accessibility?
options: Being able to run a query
Knowing what was sourced, the business rules used for transformations and the lineage information
Being added to a user group
questions.explanation: Visibility encompasses understanding aspects such as what was sourced, the business rules for transformations, metadata, golden record formulas, data quality methods, loading approaches, SLAs and lineage.

questions.stem: Which data loading approaches are mentioned as part of Visibility?
questions.explanation: Visibility includes knowing the data loading approaches, for example CDC, batch or real-time.

questions.stem: What are the Three Golden Rules of implementing a solution?
questions.explanation: The Three Golden Rules of implementing a solution are Visibility, Accessibility and Maintainability.

questions.stem: Why is it important to distinguish Accessibility from Visibility?
options: Because they refer to different database vendors
Because although often used interchangeably in simple terms, in data solutions they mean different things
Because Accessibility applies only to cloud systems
Because Visibility is a legal term
Because Accessibility is measured in gigabytes
questions.explanation: Accessibility and Visibility are often used interchangeably in simple terms, but in the world of data solutions it is crucial to distinguish between them.

questions.stem: Which types of metadata are named as part of Visibility?
questions.explanation: Visibility includes knowing about the presence of business, technical or operational metadata.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as an element of Visibility?
options: The salary of the database administrator
questions.explanation: Golden record formulas, data quality assurance methods, SLAs and lineage information all contribute to Visibility; the administrator's salary does not.

questions.stem: In the example where you ask datastore owners to extract source data and transform it for decision-making, which two concepts come into play?
questions.explanation: When you request the datastore owners to extract and transform data for decision-making, the two key concepts that come into play are Accessibility and Visibility.
